subject: TenantBurst pilot capacity intake & rollout roadmap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@tenantburst.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: TenantBurst pilot capacity intake & rollout roadmap

Hi Ari —

Great talking yesterday. To make our pilot sizing call productive, I attached a short CSV with the fields we typically need. Can you and the engineering lead fill in the rough numbers below (even ballpark is fine):

- Primary endpoints (e.g., /chat, /summarize) and percent of total traffic per endpoint
- Average prompt length (tokens) and average generated response length (tokens) per endpoint
- Session duration / conversation turn count (if applicable)
- Peak concurrent sessions or streams (approx 99th pct window) and expected sustained RPS
- Burst shape: single-minute peak, 5-min sustained peak, and daily high-hour multiplier
- Fraction of calls that require streaming vs non-streaming
- Percent of requests that use retrieval/RAG (affects KV cache & memory)
- Error/SLA tolerance (p99 latency target, acceptable error budget)

If it's easier, send a small sample of telemetry export — we can ingest it and produce a quick sizing sketch.

High-level suggestion for the pilot: start with a 2-week canary at ~25% of peak traffic behind a single-VM reserved GPU (to validate latency and token egress), then expand to reserved capacity buckets if steady-state numbers justify it. We'll also recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts and an autoscale window we can tune during the pilot.

I've cc'd Marissa and Karthik to help with commitment/technical mapping.

Attachments: tenantburst_sizing_template.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com]

Jordan —

Thanks, attached is a quick telemetry dump and a partially filled version of your CSV. Quick answers inline:

- Endpoints: /chat (60%), /batch-embed (25%), /summarize (15%)
- Prompt avg tokens: chat=140, batch-embed=60, summarize=80
- Resp avg tokens: chat=420, batch-embed=16 (embeddings), summarize=160
- Session turns: chat avg 6 turns (~1.5 min per session), many sessions are short (single-turn)
- Current peak: ~520 concurrent chat sessions during 12:00–13:00 PST (we see minute spikes up to ~740). Sustained RPS at peak hour ~180; single-minute spikes to ~300.
- Streaming: ~30% of chat traffic uses streaming responses
- RAG usage: ~40% of chat calls hit retrieval (we store per-session context in our vector DB)
- p99 latency target: <350ms ideally; we can accept p99 up to 600ms during early pilot.

Open questions for you:
1) How does Redwood account for streaming sessions when calculating concurrency vs GPU occupancy?
2) For RAG-heavy requests, what's the recommended KV-cache footprint estimate per session?
3) If we commit to a 6-month reserved pool, what discount bands do you offer and how are burst credits handled?

Attached: tb_metrics_snapshot.json (7MB), tenantburst_sizing_template_filled.csv (5KB)

Best,
Ari Kaplan
VP, Engineering — TenantBurst
ari@tenantburst.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@tenantburst.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TenantBurst pilot capacity intake & rollout roadmap

Ari —

This is perfect, thanks for the snapshot and the numbers. Quick answers to your questions and a proposed pilot cadence below.

1) Streaming & concurrency: we dimension streaming sessions by sustained NVMe/KV footprint plus open socket count. For sizing, we convert streaming sessions to an \"effective GPU token throughput\" value: streaming sessions that produce X tokens/sec are mapped to equivalent non-streaming token-rate so we can schedule batching efficiently. Practically, we recommend treating streaming requests as 1.4x the token CPU cost of non-streaming for planning purposes (this factors in smaller microbatches and higher scheduler overhead).

2) KV cache footprint: for your RAG profile (~40% retrieval) expect ~40–120MB/session depending on doc chunk size. On a 48GB GPU this typically limits concurrent RAG sessions to ~300–900 before evictions start — exact number depends on embedding dimensionality and chunking. We'll run a quick estimation pass with your tb_metrics_snapshot to give a tighter number.

3) Reserved pricing bands: I'll let Marissa share the latest tier list, but ballpark discounts start at 18% for 6-month min-commit and improve with larger commitments and prepayment. Burst credits: we offer a small monthly burst pool tied to the reserved tier (optionally purchasable as add-on).

Proposed pilot plan (conservative):
- Week 0: Dry run with 1-VM reserved GPU, smoke tests, perf baseline with sample telemetry
- Weeks 1–2: Canary at ~40% of your observed sustained peak (target 72 RPS sustained, allow 250 RPS spike testing). Monitor p50/p95/p99 and token egress.
- Weeks 3–4: Scale to reserved pool of 3 GPUs (mixed SKU) and validate RAG saturation, streaming ratios. Test prefix caching and warm KV hits.
- Post-pilot: Produce a recommendation for reserved capacity and an ops runbook for degradation fallbacks (model fallback to smaller variant + region routing).

Next steps: I'll run the snapshot against our sizing tool and share a draft capacity sketch by EOD tomorrow. Marissa — can you send the current reserved-tier sheet and any payment/contract notes? Karthik — want to schedule a 45-minute pilot sizing call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks —
Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
